title: Which pairs of these lines look as if they never meet?
description: Nine line segments are drawn: some upright, some flat, and some leaning one way or the other. The board sorts them into groups that keep the same gap and so appear parallel. Keeko then shows parallel lines in the edges of a sheet of paper and in artwork.
teaching_notes: One idea: lines that keep the same gap and never meet, however far they are extended, are parallel. Watch for students who call a flat line and an upright line parallel because both follow the grid.

source: Nine segments a to i are drawn on a grid. a, h and i are upright. c and g are flat. d and f lean one way. b and e lean the other way. Which pairs of lines appear to be parallel?
video_script.why: The child sorts lines into groups by whether they keep the same gap, and meets the name parallel for lines that never meet.
video_script.substitution: The book's own question about the lines in the figure: which pairs of lines appear to be parallel, with parallel lines defined as lines that do not meet however far they are extended.
video_script.anchor: Nine line segments named a to i on a grid: a, h and i upright; c and g flat; d and f leaning one way; b and e leaning the other way.
video_script.payoff_line: The upright segments are parallel, and so are the flat ones and each set of leaning ones.

final_answer.value: a, h and i; c and g; d and f; b and e
final_answer.spoken: eigh, h and i; c and g; d and f; and b and e

hold_back: a, h and i; c and g; d and f; b and e
maths_rules: upright segments a, h and i keep the same gap, so they appear parallel
flat segments c and g appear parallel
d and f lean one way, each along the diagonal of a square, and appear parallel
b and e lean the other way, also along the diagonal of a square, and appear parallel
a flat segment and an upright one cross, so they are not parallel
video_script.design: The nine segments stay on the stage. Each group lights up in its own colour as the board names it, and the flat and upright segments are shown crossing at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about nine line segments on a grid.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They are named from eigh to i. Some stand upright, some lie flat, and some lean.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Which pairs of these lines look as if they would never meet?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.m1: two lines are extended at both ends and never meet
marks.m2: the same gap is marked at two places along them

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Two lines that never meet, however far we extend them at both ends, are called parallel lines.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Parallel lines keep the same gap all along.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We look for the segments that keep the same gap.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Look at the opposite edges of a sheet of paper.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Parallel lines are often used in artwork and shading. Look around your classroom and spot some.
